channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: One in Three Kyrgyz Workers Faced Workplace Violence, Study Reveals
item.description: A recent study indicates that 37% of working residents in Kyrgyzstan experienced at least one form of violence or harassment at work in the past year. These include humiliation, psychological pressure, and sexual harassment. Nearly half of those affected chose not to report their experiences due to fear of repercussions or ineffectiveness of complaints.

item.title: Kazakhstani Man Earns $2 Million Monthly Using Artificial Intelligence for Video
item.description: A young man from Kazakhstan is reportedly earning 2 million tenge per month by creating advertising videos using artificial intelligence. Initially making videos as a joke for friends, he now undertakes international projects and has developed his own production. He faced health challenges after a large film project.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Development Bank Supports Women Entrepreneurs with Green Financing
item.description: The Development Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic is supporting women's entrepreneurial initiatives through a green financing program for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises. The program targets businesses where women are founders, co-owners, or managers, aiming to promote equal opportunities and sustainable business growth while adhering to environmental standards.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Cleans Three Water Bodies, Removing 372 km of Fishing Nets and Over 25 Tons of Trash
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has removed 372.4 km of synthetic fishing nets and over 25 tons of garbage from Issyk-Kul, Son-Kul, and the Toktogul reservoir. The collected waste was transported to a recycling plant in Bishkek for disposal. These clean-up efforts are being conducted under the President's directive, involving divers, police, and environmental specialists.

item.title: Two Military Leaders Arrested in Connection with Mi-8 Helicopter Crash
item.description: The former head of the Air Assault Defense Forces and the commander of military unit No. 23565 have been arrested in connection with the crash of a Mi-8 military helicopter in 2024. The arrests were made based on investigation materials and expert conclusions. The crash resulted in one fatality and injuries to ten servicemen, causing state losses exceeding 50 million soms.

item.title: France Denounces Taliban Policies as Gender Apartheid, Rules Out Recognition
item.description: France's Foreign Minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, has labeled the Taliban's policies against women and girls as 'gender apartheid.' He emphasized that technical discussions with the group do not signify recognition or endorsement of their rule. Barrot stated that France has no intention of establishing diplomatic relations with the Taliban, who he described as enforcing the worst form of discrimination against women and girls in the modern era.

item.title: Underwater Dump: Kyrgyzstan Removes 372 Kilometers of Fishing Nets from Lakes
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has removed over 372 kilometers of synthetic fishing nets and more than 25 tons of garbage from Issyk-Kul, Son-Kul lakes, and the Toktogul reservoir. The operation, ordered by President Sadyr Japarov, involved divers from the Ministry of Emergency Situations, environmental police, and the Ministry of Natural Resources. All retrieved materials were sent for recycling in Bishkek.

item.title: Two Military Leaders Detained in Kyrgyzstan Mi-8 Helicopter Crash Investigation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's military prosecutor has detained two former military leaders in connection with the January 2024 crash of a Mi-8 helicopter. The detentions are part of an ongoing criminal investigation into the incident, which resulted in one fatality and ten injuries. The state incurred over 50 million soms in damages.

item.title: Atyrau Refinery to Replace 'Stinky Pond' with New Evaporation Pond for Land Reclamation
item.description: The Atyrau Refinery has begun designing a new 500-hectare evaporation pond to complete the reclamation of 'Tukhla Balka,' a major source of unpleasant odors in Atyrau. This large settling pond, used since 1945 for refinery and sewage discharge, is being remediated to address environmental concerns.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Jail Time for Damaging Border Fences
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering introducing criminal liability for intentional damage to border fences, with penalties up to five years imprisonment. Fines are proposed for accidental damage, including by livestock. The bill aims to address frequent damage, often for illegal cattle herding or smuggling.

item.title: Belarus President Offers to Guarantee Security for Zelensky in Moscow Talks
item.description: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko stated he is ready to fly to Moscow with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as a security guarantor. He believes a trilateral format involving Belarus, Ukraine, and Russia could resolve the conflict faster than European involvement, emphasizing their shared Slavic heritage.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Perform Complex Vascular Anomaly Surgeries on Children
item.description: Kazakhstan is implementing a new high-tech method for treating children with complex vascular malformations. Previously, patients requiring specific types of this medical care were sent abroad for treatment. This initiative aims to provide advanced medical services domestically.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Establishes New Department for Migration Affairs
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will implement an experimental labor migration and citizenship regulation regime starting January 1, 2027, until December 31, 2027. A new Department for Migration Affairs will be created under the Ministry of Labor, Social Security, and Migration to handle residency permits, foreign citizen registration, and migration control.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Remaining Oil Reserves Estimated at Over 4 Billion Tons
item.description: Kazakhstan's subsoil holds over 4 billion tons of extractable oil reserves as of January 1, 2026. The Atyrau region accounts for the largest share, with 3.1 billion tons. Other significant reserves are located in the Mangystau and Aktobe regions. The Ministry of Industry and Construction provided these figures.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economic Growth Outpaces Purchasing Power, Experts Warn
item.description: While Kazakhstan's economy has grown significantly, with average wages rising, the purchasing power of the tenge has declined. Experts note that despite higher nominal incomes, increased living costs mean citizens can buy less than before. The National Bureau of Economic Research highlighted this trend with an example of income versus expenditure.

item.title: Hungarian Prime Minister Makes Historic First Visit to Ukraine for Talks with Zelensky
item.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Szijjarto called his meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Uzhhorod a "historic event." This marks the first visit by the Hungarian government head to Ukraine in over a decade. Szijjarto expressed Hungary's condemnation of Russia's nearly five-year war against Ukraine.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Introduces New Wage Coefficients for Mine Workers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has established new regional coefficients for the salaries of employees at gold mining enterprises and the Sary-Jaz tin deposit. The decision aims to provide additional compensation for workers in high-altitude and remote areas. These new coefficients will be funded by the enterprises themselves, with no state budget allocation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Administration Reports Over 28 Billion Som Revenue
item.description: The Presidential Administration of Kyrgyzstan reported a total revenue of over 28 billion som for the first nine months of 2026. This figure exceeded the planned target by more than 4.2 billion som, achieving 117.8% of the plan. Revenue increased by 29.9% compared to the same period in 2025.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Builds Two New Bitumen Bases to Boost Road Construction Material Reserves
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has constructed two new bitumen bases to increase its reserves of road construction materials, bringing the total storage capacity to 34,000 tons. Previously, the country could store only 14,000 tons. The new facilities in Shamaldy-Sai and Kemin each have a capacity of 10,000 tons.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Strong Tenge: Experts Warn of Risks Over Potential Benefits
item.description: Experts suggest Kazakhstan's national currency strengthening, supported by external factors, has increased risks more than profits. A strong tenge makes imports cheaper and domestic products less competitive due to higher costs. While the tenge reached a yearly high in August, strengthening by 16-17% against the dollar, it hasn't boosted real incomes as domestic prices remained high.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Trains Laboratory Specialists in GMO Detection
item.description: Laboratory specialists in Kyrgyzstan have enhanced their practical skills in detecting genetically modified organisms (GMOs) in food products and agricultural raw materials. A specialized practical training on GMO detection using the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) method concluded at the Institute of Biotechnology. Participants learned international ISO standards and EAEU technical regulations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan May Change Residency Admission Procedures
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering introducing a unified entrance exam for residency admissions and determining the number of available positions based on the country's medical personnel needs. The Ministry of Health is developing a digital mechanism to identify the demand for doctors by specialty and region. These changes aim to align medical specialist training with actual needs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Uncover Over 440 Extortion Cases in 10 Months
item.description: Kazakhstan's police identified over 440 cases of extortion between January and October, averaging nearly 1.5 incidents daily. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that victims included entrepreneurs and educational institutions. Additionally, 50 cases were initiated against organized crime groups during the same period.

item.title: Zelensky: US Wants Agreement on Ukraine by January
item.description: US negotiators are pushing for a peace agreement to end the war in Ukraine by December or January, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky. He stated that Kyiv also desires a swift end to the conflict but not at the expense of Ukraine's interests. Zelensky emphasized the need for continued sanctions against Russia if Moscow does not wish to end the war.

item.title: 175 Migrants Missing After Setting Sail from Senegal to Europe
item.description: Approximately 175 migrants are missing in the Atlantic Ocean after their boat departed from Senegal for Europe. Contact with the vessel was lost two weeks ago. The wooden boat left Dakar's port area around November 9-10. Senegalese authorities and human rights groups are calling for intensified search and rescue operations.

item.title: Bishkek Residents Sue State Mortgage Company Over Housing Project Access Road
item.description: Residents of two buildings in Bishkek are suing the State Mortgage Company (GIK) and contractors over a planned access road for a new housing complex. The proposed road would pass through the courtyards of existing buildings, which residents claim is illegal. They initially sought demolition but now focus on disputing the road's legality.

item.title: New Transport Corridors with China Offer Tajikistan Reduced Costs and Trade Growth
item.description: Developing new road and rail corridors with China presents Tajikistan with opportunities to cut transport costs, expand foreign trade, and leverage its transit potential. The Eurasian Development Bank highlights two key routes: a multimodal corridor to Europe via Tajikistan and the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway.

item.title: US Congress Members Urge Trump to Withdraw Invitation to Putin for Miami G20 Summit
item.description: Twenty bipartisan members of the U.S. House of Representatives have urged President Donald Trump to withdraw an invitation to Russian President Vladimir Putin for the G20 summit in Miami this December. Citing the war in Ukraine and alleged Russian intelligence sharing with Iran, they stated America will not welcome Putin.

item.title: Prosecutor's Office Restores Social Guarantees for 74 Workers After Unpaid Contributions
item.description: The prosecutor's office in West Kazakhstan region has restored social guarantees for 74 employees of a utility company. The company failed to transfer mandatory pension contributions and social payments totaling approximately 4 million tenge by submitting false tax declarations. The prosecutor's office intervened to rectify the violations.

item.title: US Jury Finds Huawei Guilty of Conspiracy to Steal Trade Secrets
item.description: A jury in New York has found Chinese company Huawei guilty of charges including bank fraud related to its business in Iran and the theft of trade secrets from U.S. companies. The verdict was delivered following a trial concerning the company's alleged illicit activities.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Approves 2027 Budget with $51 Billion Deficit
item.description: Saudi Arabia has approved its 2027 budget, projecting a deficit of approximately $51 billion. The finance minister stated the economy can withstand a prolonged conflict. Projected revenues are 1.2 trillion Saudi riyals, with expenditures at 1.39 trillion riyals.

item.title: Afghan Fresh Fruit Exports Plummet 88% Amidst Rising Trade Through Central Asia
item.description: Afghanistan's fresh fruit exports fell 88% by weight from April to September 2026, despite a more than doubling of goods shipped through Central Asia to $210 million. Pakistan's border closure significantly impacted fruit exports, with increased reliance on Central Asian routes.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan Launch Trans-Caspian Digital Cable, Bypassing Russia
item.description: A new 380-kilometer fiber-optic cable connects Aktau, Kazakhstan, to Sumgayit, Azerbaijan, aiming to reduce Russia's digital connectivity dominance. The Trans-Caspian Fiber Optic Cable (TCFOC) has a capacity of 400 terabits per second and is part of a regional push for digital sovereignty. Kazakhstan anticipates significant transit traffic, potentially reaching 21.6 Tbps.

item.title: US Deputy Secretary of State Discusses Trans-Caspian Trade with Turkmenistan Leaders
item.description: US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met with Turkmen leaders in Ashgabat to discuss expanding trans-Caspian trade and transport routes. Discussions included potential cooperation on regional infrastructure initiatives and the development of trans-Caspian transport links. The Turkmen government noted "fruitful" bilateral contacts yielding positive results.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Mandatory Housing Insurance Against Natural Disasters
item.description: Kazakhstan is developing a mandatory housing insurance system to cover damages from earthquakes, floods, and wildfires. Property owners would pay annual contributions to a special fund, intended to provide faster aid to victims and reduce the state budget burden. Experts have mixed opinions, with some supporting the reform and others concerned about new fees.

item.title: Military Helicopter Crashes in Central Turkey, Killing Five Personnel
item.description: Five military personnel died when a military helicopter crashed in the central Turkish city of Eskişehir during a training flight. The AS-532 type helicopter belonged to the Air Force Command. The Ministry of National Defense confirmed the crash, and search and rescue operations are ongoing at the wreckage site.

item.title: Taliban Authorities Force Afghan Men to Restrict Female Family Members
item.description: Afghan men and women have reported that Taliban authorities are compelling men to impose strict restrictions on female family members. These restrictions reportedly include forbidding women from leaving their homes and withholding their cell phones. The Taliban's actions aim to enforce their interpretation of social and personal freedoms for women.

item.title: Russian Authorities Seize 27 Tons of Contaminated Tomatoes from Turkmenistan
item.description: Russia's Rosselkhoznadzor in the Omsk region has intercepted 27 tons of tomatoes from Turkmenistan infected with the Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus (ToBRFV). The contaminated shipments were detected at a temporary storage warehouse and have been returned to the supplier to prevent the spread of the disease.

item.title: RFE/RL Resumes Shortwave Broadcasts in Afghanistan with Educational Programs for Girls
item.description: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL) has returned to shortwave radio broadcasting in Afghanistan, offering new educational programming for girls excluded from school by the Taliban. The broadcasts, which began November 24, include three hours of educational content, news, analysis, and music, targeting girls aged 12-17.

item.title: Uzbek President Concludes State Visit to Jordan, Strategic Partnership Established
item.description: The state visit of the President of Uzbekistan to the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan has concluded. During the visit, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held productive talks with King Abdullah II in Amman and participated in a business forum. An agreement establishing a strategic partnership and 19 other cooperation documents were signed.
